items: I know Hangul was intentionally created, not evolved by chance.
I know consonant shapes mimic the mouth, tongue, and throat.
I can recognize the basic consonants: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅅ, ㅇ.

hangul-02.q: Which vowel sound did you hear?
Which vowel sound did you hear?

items: I can tell vertical vowels (ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅣ) from horizontal ones (ㅗ, ㅜ, ㅡ).
I can hear the difference between ㅓ and ㅗ.
I can read the six fundamental vowels.
I understand that Korean letters combine into syllable blocks.
I know whether to write the vowel to the right or below the consonant.
I can read two-letter blocks combining basic consonants and vowels.
I can recognize the five additional consonants: ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅂ, ㅈ, ㅎ.
I understand the difference between Korean ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ and English g/d/b.
I can read words like 바다 (sea) and 다리 (leg/bridge).

items: I know that adding an extra stroke adds a 'y' sound.
I can tell ㅑ, ㅕ, ㅛ, ㅠ from the base vowels.
I know ㅐ and ㅔ sound practically the same in modern Korean.

hangul-11.q: Which vowel sound did you hear?
Which vowel sound did you hear?

items: I can recognize compound vowels combining horizontal and vertical strokes.
I know ㅙ, ㅚ, and ㅞ make almost identical sounds in modern Korean.
I can read complex blocks like 과, 뭐, and 화.

items: I can hear the three-way distinction: plain, aspirated, and tense consonants.
I know double letters (ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅆ, ㅉ) represent tense sounds.
I can read words like 토끼 (rabbit) and 커피 (coffee).
I know how final consonants (받침) sit at the bottom of a syllable block.
I can distinguish 받침 sounds like ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅇ, and ㄹ.
I know ㅇ makes an 'ng' sound when placed as a 받침.

items: I understand how a final consonant slides into a following empty ㅇ block.
I can read words like 한국어 as [한구거] and 음악 as [으막].
I know that spelling stays fixed even when pronunciation connects.

hangul-09.q: Which real-life word did you hear?

items: I can read common Korean loanwords like 커피, 버스, and 택시.
I can recognize important real-world signs like 화장실.
I feel confident sounding out authentic Korean words.
